strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets a scheduled controller convert a bounded runtime drive stop into a single explicit recovery task without external stop interpretation.
Exposes the admitted recovery boundary through bounded next-action, selected task/run, replay, and stop-reason metadata a headless caller can inspect without raw content.
Requires explicit authorization and validates persisted drive-stop fingerprints before admitting any recovery task.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with persistent_structured_ledger and runtime_permission_enforcement support.
answers.new_capability: A headless.continue_once caller can admit exactly one recovery task from current persisted product-loop drive-stop evidence, with replay-safe duplicate prevention.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M59.1 can drive product-continuation routes until a closed stop, but it leaves recovery task admission to the external controller.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Scheduled automation can observe a product-loop stop but cannot ask the Rust runtime to own the next recovery task boundary.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M57/M58/M59 product-continuation admission/run/drive sequencing because this phase handles stopped drive recovery admission rather than continuing an eligible route.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.continue_once surface is extended with a bounded target; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The existing bounded continue-once result carries selected task/run, replay status, next route, and next action.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime validates drive checkpoint evidence and creates a Created recovery task with bounded decision ledger evidence while refusing stale or unauthorized requests.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A scheduled caller can recover from closed product-loop drive stops through runtime authority instead of making ad hoc external task-start decisions.
answers.milestone_progress: Implements the first M60 transition from stop observation to runtime-owned recovery task admission; execution remains a later explicit phase.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: Manifest updates are limited to selecting and archiving the current M60.1 value gate; no guard engine logic is changed.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts product_loop_stop_recovery_target only with explicit authorization
runtime validates session, drive, stop reason, end sequence, drive fingerprint, post-progress fingerprint, and next-route fingerprint when supplied
success admits one Created recovery task and returns next_action run_recovery_task_explicitly without running tools, provider, workspace apply, shell, git, network, or services
replaying the same continuation returns the same selected task/run without duplicate task creation or duplicate decision event
stale or unauthorized evidence is rejected before task admission
behavior_evidence: Behavior test headless_continue_admits_product_loop_stop_recovery_from_drive_evidence_and_replays validates successful recovery admission, replay without duplicate task/event creation, stale evidence denial, authorization denial, and no TaskRunning side effect.
Validation covers cargo test --workspace, cargo check --workspace, cargo fmt --check, diagnostics guard, phase-value guard, and diff check.

accepted_capability: Runtime can admit exactly one Created recovery task from current product-loop drive-stop evidence through headless.continue_once.
Replay returns the same selected task/run and does not duplicate task creation or decision ledger events.
behavior_evidence: Behavior test headless_continue_admits_product_loop_stop_recovery_from_drive_evidence_and_replays validates successful recovery admission, replay without duplicate task/event creation, stale evidence denial, authorization denial, and no TaskRunning side effect.
Validation covers cargo test --workspace, cargo check --workspace, cargo fmt --check, diagnostics guard, phase-value guard, and diff check.
safety_boundary: Recovery admission requires explicit product_loop_stop_recovery authorization.
Runtime validates drive fingerprint, stop reason, end session sequence, post-progress fingerprint, and optional route fingerprint before mutation.
Admission does not run provider, tools, workspace apply, shell, git, network, or services.
non_goals: Does not execute the admitted recovery task.
Does not add a JSON-RPC method, report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, or summary wrapper.
Does not interpret raw prompts, raw provider output, raw file content, stdout, stderr, commands, or environment values into ledger payloads.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected a stop-inspection wrapper because it would not create runtime-owned recovery capacity.
Rejected automatic recovery execution because M60.1 only admits an explicit recovery task boundary.
Rejected external controller task.start choreography because it bypasses runtime evidence validation for the stopped drive.
technical_debt: The explicit next route reuses the existing run-product-continuation route kind while next_action identifies recovery execution; a future phase can introduce a dedicated recovery run route if it materially improves execution semantics.
next_capability_rationale: Next capability should run the admitted recovery task explicitly with fresh stop-evidence validation and bounded context, preserving the no-auto-run invariant.
